-->## Why

The original Copilot canvas vertical slice depended on canonical Agent Host Protocol additions and microsoft/agent-host-protocol#472. This version preserves the complete local canvas experience while remaining independently reviewable and shippable from VS Code: the effective diff contains no canvas-specific changes under `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/**`.

## Architecture

### Durable local Copilot runtime

Trusted, durable local Copilot sessions always request standalone extensions and the canvas renderer. Ephemeral sessions request neither, and remote or unsupported Agent Hosts expose no canvas capability. Workspace Trust and the existing AI-feature entitlement gate remain authoritative.

The release-aligned Copilot runtime, extension bootstrap, and extension SDK paths are resolved once per Copilot client residency in `copilotAgent.ts`. The resolved SDK path is carried into create/resume launch plans; `CopilotSessionLauncher` no longer searches application `node_modules` per session. Missing required runtime assets fail visibly.

Project extensions receive canonical launch admission, a stable private `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR`, and extension readiness before the relevant model turn.

### Typed VS Code-private transport

`agentHostExtensionProtocol.ts` defines the versioned local extension boundary:

- capability: `vscode.canvases.v1`
- full-replacement notification: `vscode/canvases/v1/changed`
- exact revision-fenced RPC: `vscode/canvases/v1/resolveSource`

The local service/client validates every payload and fails closed. `protocolServerHandler.ts` retains the latest per-chat snapshot in process memory, replays it after initialize, clears it when the session disappears, and resolves only the exact advertised canvas/revision/source tuple. Remote connections never advertise the extension.

The runtime projection preserves live identity, availability, revisions, duplicate suppression, the eight-canvas limit, URL log redaction, ignored resume replay, restart non-restoration, and visible extension-started turns with tools, approvals, usage, responses, errors, cancellation, and completion.

### Provider-neutral Sessions presentation

Shared Sessions contracts expose provider-neutral canvas metadata and source resolution. The Agent Host provider maps the private transport into those contracts; Sessions UI does not import Copilot or transport-specific implementations.

Canvases use private, unlisted BrowserViews. They automatically reveal when opened, dismiss when no longer available, preserve accessibility help/focus behavior, and remain absent from the ordinary Integrated Browser list.

### Canvas authoring and reload

The built-in `/create-canvas` skill authors project extensions under `.github/extensions/`, uses `@github/copilot-sdk/extension`, reloads providers, and verifies the result through `list_canvas_capabilities`, `open_canvas`, and canvas actions rather than the Integrated Browser.

The eager local-Copilot `extensions_reload` tool calls the live `session.extensions.reload()` RPC. Existing open canvas instances become temporarily unavailable while providers restart, then are rehydrated by the runtime. Extension process memory is not preserved; durable data belongs in `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR`, workspace files, or another persistent store.

Customization routing normalizes `agent-host-<provider>` and `remote-<authority>-<provider>` schemes back to their logical provider before applying `sessionTypes`, allowing the contributed `copilotcli` skill to reach local and remote Agent Host customization sync correctly.

## Enablement simplification

There is no canvas preview setting or Copilot restart-on-setting-change path. Durable local Copilot sessions always admit the runtime; ephemeral and remote sessions remain unsupported. This removes mirrored configuration, dynamic snapshot/source invalidation, provider/UI setting checks, and restart coordination while preserving the meaningful security boundaries.

## Reviewable commit history

1. `425d703741d` — `browser: refactor: extract reusable web contents view host`

5. `af0118e7fe7` — `copilot: feat: add create-canvas authoring workflow`

The canonical-AHP add/remove sequence was collapsed into the final private-transport implementation. The unrelated side-panel editor-preservation fix was removed from this PR and is available separately on `ulugbekna/preserve-editors-side-panel-toggle` (`adc856dcaae`). The cloud-model vendor change and unrelated MCP-backgrounding drift are also absent.

## OSS verification

Live Code OSS verification used the chess canvas in `~/code/test`:

- opened and automatically revealed the canvas;
- played `e2` to `e4`;
- projected the extension-started agent turn into the owning chat;
- invoked `get_state` and `make_move`;
- rendered the agent's `c7` to `c5` response and persisted the game privately.

The authoring/reload flow was also verified live:

- raw `/create-canvas` invoked the synced skill and requested the intended canvas behavior before creating files;
- `extensions_reload` made a newly authored Kanban canvas discoverable;
- `open_canvas` opened it as a normal Sessions canvas rather than in Integrated Browser;
- an already-open instance remained actionable after a second reload without another `open_canvas` call.

![Chess canvas and visible provider-started turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a559aeb4-2459-47d7-999a-7737e14d8bc5)

## Tradeoffs versus canonical AHP

This deliberately trades cross-client interoperability for standalone delivery and a smaller review surface. A canonical AHP implementation would make canvas capability/state/source resolution available to every conforming host and client, but requires coordinated schema, generated-client, version, and external repository changes. The private VS Code extension is typed and versioned, but only VS Code local Agent Host clients understand it.

Snapshots are process-resident and are not restored after an Agent Host restart, matching the intended product behavior. Closing a Sessions canvas editor is presentation-only and does not close the runtime instance. The pinned Copilot runtime still requires `extensionSdkPath` whenever standalone extensions are requested; this PR cleans up ownership of that path rather than removing the runtime requirement.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The awaited call path from first-send materialization to the explicit 10-second timeout is direct and covered by a test; only the prevalence of slowly starting extensions is uncertain, not the mechanism or maximum delay.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Copilot runtime IPC calls and extension provider subprocess startup
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay is paid once for every durable local Copilot session materialization; when any discovered extension is still starting, initialization waits for that provider event for up to 10 seconds before the first turn can proceed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked critical path and increased first-turn latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Durable session configs forced `requestExtensions: false`, and `initializeSession()` did not list extensions, wait for provider startup, or list canvases before registering the session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: All non-ephemeral sessions now request extensions/canvas rendering, and `initializeSession()` synchronously awaits `_waitForCanvasExtensions`; that helper crosses two runtime RPC boundaries and waits up to 10 seconds whenever an extension reports `starting`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 2747 awaits `_waitForCanvasExtensions(wrapper)` inside `initializeSession`; added lines 2768-2771 call `rpc.extensions.list()` and await `raceTimeout(..., 10_000)`. The launcher diff also changes `requestExtensions` from false to true for every durable session.
Findings.Title: Keep extension readiness off generic session initialization
Findings.Impact: In a workspace with a project/user extension that starts slowly or fails to emit readiness promptly, even a normal non-canvas first prompt is held for as long as 10 seconds before the session is registered and the turn starts.
Findings.Evidence: `CopilotAgent._materializeProvisional` awaits `_initializeAndRegisterSession` immediately before the first send, and `_initializeAndRegisterSession` awaits `session.initializeSession()`. The new test `observes extension readiness events that race with the status snapshot` confirms session creation remains pending while a project extension is `starting`. The runtime launch provider executes each admitted extension via `process.execPath`, so this wait includes real subprocess startup rather than local bookkeeping.
Findings.Recommendation: Start extension discovery/readiness in the background (ideally earlier than first-send materialization) and join it only for canvas-dependent work, or otherwise move this bounded wait off generic `initializeSession()` while preserving readiness before a canvas provider is actually consumed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The manual refresh call path, per-parent command placement, 2,000-node bound, and 32-command batch concurrency are explicit. Exact page tree shape and command duration affect magnitude only.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Chrome DevTools Protocol IPC requests and AX node response objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One Accessible View refresh sends one `Accessibility.getChildAXNodes` command for every expandable AX node encountered, up to the 2,000-node cap, in bursts of 32 concurrent commands.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Accessible View latency, IPC load, and allocation/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Session canvases had no Accessible View snapshot path, so opening or refreshing this view issued no CDP accessibility traversal.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new traversal starts at the root and fetches each parent's children through a separate CDP command, waiting batch-by-batch before it can format and display the snapshot.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 36 invokes `sendCommand('Accessibility.getChildAXNodes', { id })` inside `parentIds.map`; the surrounding loop repeats this for every queued parent until 2,000 nodes are retained.
Findings.Title: Fetch the accessibility tree without per-parent CDP calls
Findings.Impact: On a realistic complex canvas with hundreds or thousands of semantic containers, opening Accessible View can require hundreds to nearly 2,000 CDP round trips before any content appears, making an accessibility workflow noticeably slow while bursting main/renderer IPC.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionCanvasEditor.refreshSemanticContent()` awaits `model.getAccessibilitySnapshot()` on the Accessible View critical path, which crosses workbench-to-main IPC and reaches this loop. The test explicitly asserts separate child commands for successive parents. The repository's existing web-content extractor uses the bulk `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` CDP command instead, proving a non-per-parent boundary exists.
Findings.Recommendation: Use the existing bulk AX-tree command for the main frame (with depth/retained-node and 32 KiB output bounds), or another subtree-batching strategy, so the snapshot requires a bounded small number of CDP calls rather than one per parent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a durable local Copilot session and send the first model turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First-send materialization awaits extension-root admission, SDK session launch, `initializeSession()`, extension readiness, canvas listing, and remaining session setup before the session is registered and the turn can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize each admitted project-extension root with `fs.realpath`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per file-scheme working/additional directory per session initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No project-extension launch admission or root canonicalization occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before SDK session initialization starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch admitted standalone extension providers through `process.execPath` and `extension_bootstrap.mjs`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one subprocess per discovered admitted extension for each runtime-managed provider lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session config forced standalone extensions off, so these provider subprocesses were not requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A provider that remains `starting` keeps generic session initialization waiting up to 10 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List extension statuses, wait for extension-loaded notification, then list canvases through Copilot SDK RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two RPC requests per durable session, plus one readiness event wait when any extension reports `starting`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension/canvas readiness RPCs were on session initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly awaited by `initializeSession()` on first-send materialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initialization per durable session; filesystem work scales with workspace roots, while readiness delay scales with the slowest discovered starting extension and is capped at 10 seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace roots are canonicalized sequentially. Runtime extension providers may start independently, but this code joins them through one readiness event and one fixed timeout; no host-side global limiter was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Bundled runtime/SDK paths are resolved once per Copilot client residency and the extension SDK path is held in a WeakMap. Extension status is queried anew per session; settled extensions avoid the timeout but still incur extension-list and canvas-list RPCs. Failures are not negative-cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the first-send call path and awaited timeout are direct and covered by a readiness-race test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The proportion of sessions with project/user extensions and their startup duration is unknown; the explicit 10-second upper bound makes the worst-case latency concrete.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression because canvas provider startup is placed on every durable session's generic first-turn critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive canvas snapshots and automatically open live canvas editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A runtime canvas event is projected through the Agent Host process and local protocol notification, updates Sessions observables, auto-opens an editor, resolves the source over RPC, creates an unlisted BrowserView over workbench/main IPC, and navigates it to the HTTP(S) source.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast and receive bounded full-replacement canvas snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification per changed chat snapshot per capable local client, carrying at most eight canvases; equal snapshots are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Drives editor presentation but does not itself wait on network or disk.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the exact canvas source through workbench client, Agent Host protocol, and provider service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per canvas revision that is loaded into an editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The editor cannot create/navigate its BrowserView until this completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create, lay out, show, and capture an unlisted Electron WebContentsView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One BrowserView per opened canvas editor; only visible models continue the inherited one-second screenshot cadence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas editors did not create BrowserViews; the screenshot mechanism itself already existed for Integrated Browser views.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation and initial navigation are awaited before canvas content is attached; periodic screenshots are off initial load but consume IPC/encoding while visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate the ephemeral BrowserView to the resolved HTTP(S) canvas URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per loaded canvas revision, with normal page subresource fan-out determined by the canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Page loading controls when interactive canvas content appears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most eight projected canvases per chat; reconnect snapshots can contain all eight, while live open events usually add one at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The service invokes `openEditor` without awaiting it for every newly ready canvas, so up to eight opens can be in flight; actual editor-group serialization is internal and not established. BrowserView creation/navigation is otherwise per opened canvas.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Snapshots are full replacements and deduplicated at protocol boundaries. Presented revisions suppress duplicate editor opens. BrowserViews use ephemeral sessions and are recreated for a new revision; source URLs are resolved exactly per revision and are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and boundary count; lower for actual parallel BrowserView creation because editor-service scheduling is internal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of extensions opening several canvases at once and the cost of each page are unknown; the hard eight-canvas limit bounds the burst.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: work is required by explicitly opened canvases, duplicate suppression and an eight-item cap bound it, and effective heavyweight concurrency was not proven beyond the service calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh Accessible View for an active canvas
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible View calls `SessionCanvasEditor.refreshSemanticContent`, awaits workbench-to-main IPC, attaches the Electron debugger, traverses the main-frame AX tree through CDP, formats up to 32 KiB, then emits the semantic-content change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request an accessibility snapshot from renderer/workbench to Electron main.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One main-process request per Accessible View refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas Accessible View did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Accessible content remains in a reading state until it resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enable Accessibility, fetch the root, fetch each parent's children via CDP, and disable Accessibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four fixed commands plus up to roughly 2,000 per-parent child commands, in batches of 32.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No CDP AX traversal occurred for session canvases; existing repository extraction uses bulk `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` per frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All batches complete before semantic text is shown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Expandable accessibility nodes in the main frame, capped at 2,000 retained nodes; command count approaches one per expandable node rather than one per snapshot.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Child requests are issued in batches of 32 with a barrier between batches; there is no coalescing of concurrent refresh requests, though sequence checks discard stale results.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No AX snapshot cache is retained. Each refresh performs a cold traversal; navigation invalidates semantic text and the next refresh repeats all commands.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the critical path, command placement, cap, and batching are direct and test-asserted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual AX tree size and per-command latency vary by canvas, but complex application canvases commonly contain hundreds of semantic containers and the algorithmic fan-out is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out because a single accessibility refresh can require hundreds to nearly 2,000 serialized-batch CDP round trips.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the canvas extension reload tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A model tool call awaits one live SDK `extensions.reload()` RPC; the Copilot runtime stops and restarts every extension provider before returning the tool result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload all extensions in the current Copilot SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One aggregate SDK RPC per explicit `extensions_reload` tool invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension reload tool or runtime reload RPC was exposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only the explicit reload tool result and canvas availability during provider restart.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop and restart extension provider processes as part of the SDK reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Runtime-defined, scaling with installed session extensions but grouped behind one host RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No host-triggered extension provider restart path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Intentional critical work for the reload operation, not ordinary turn startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and startup/cleanup cost of extensions in the current session; invocation frequency is controlled by model/tool use rather than ordinary turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider restart concurrency is owned by the SDK and not visible here; the host awaits one aggregate reload RPC and does not issue per-extension calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No reload-result cache is appropriate because the operation intentionally re-reads changed extension files; failures are surfaced and subsequent calls retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the aggregate RPC and intended restart semantics; internal provider scheduling is opaque.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count and restart duration are runtime-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the expensive boundary is explicit, user/model-triggered reload work and is already grouped into one RPC rather than host-side per-extension fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across startup, canvas transport/UI lifecycle, BrowserView rendering, accessibility extraction, and reload boundaries. Reported the generic first-turn extension-readiness wait and per-parent CDP accessibility fan-out; other boundary work is bounded, deduplicated, inherited without material amplification, or intrinsic to explicit canvas operations.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
